steps.title: Why write a sonnet?
steps.body: Traditionally about love. Using sonnet form signals: this is serious, this is about love, this connects to poetic tradition.

steps.title: Golden Rule
steps.body: Naming a technique scores zero marks. You must explain its EFFECT.

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: In poetry analysis questions, AO2 (language, form, structure) typically carries 30-36 marks. Name the technique, quote precisely, then explain the effect — this three-step sequence is the minimum for each analytical point. Aim for 3-4 developed technique discussions in a 30-mark response.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is enjambment and what effect can it create? | What's the difference between a caesura and an end-stopped line? | What are the features of a Shakespearean sonnet?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Enjambment is when a sentence runs over the end of a line without punctuation. Effects: creates forward momentum, links ideas, reflects continuous action or thought, sounds natural and conversational. | Caesura is a pause WITHIN a line (usually with punctuation). End-stopped lines have punctuation AT the end. Caesura slows within the line; end-stopped lines complete the thought before the next. | Shakespearean sonnet: 14 lines, iambic pentameter, ABAB CDCD EFEF GG rhyme scheme. Three quatrains present problem; final couplet provides resolution or twist.
